questions.question: What is "The American Dream"?
options: The idea that anyone in the USA can achieve success through hard work
A law that guarantees everyone a job
questions.explanation: The American Dream is the idea that everyone, regardless of background, can succeed through hard work. It has attracted immigrants for centuries.

questions.question: What do critics say about the American Dream?
options: It is not equally available to everyone because of factors like race, class and economy
It is too easy to achieve
questions.explanation: Critics argue that race, class and economic background give people very different starting points, so the dream is not equally available to all.

questions.question: Why is the USA often called a diverse or multicultural country?
options: Because people from all over the world have immigrated there for centuries
Because it has many different climates
Because every state has its own language
Because it has two official religions
questions.explanation: Centuries of immigration from all over the world have made the USA a country of great cultural diversity.

questions.question: How has American culture influenced the rest of the world?
options: Through films, music, food and technology that spread globally
It has had almost no influence outside the USA
questions.explanation: American culture - Hollywood films, popular music, fast food and tech companies - has enormous global influence.

questions.question: The USA is divided into how many states?
questions.explanation: The USA consists of 50 states. It started with 13 colonies, and Alaska and Hawaii became the last two states in 1959.
